ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure is a circular traffic sign, with a circular border on the outside, and four dark arc-shaped regions inside; these dark regions are separated by the light-colored diagonal cross-shaped part and the light-colored part of the outer ring. The problem states that each dark region is one fourth of some circle. Reasoning: Let the radius of the circle to which each dark quarter circle belongs be r. The 4 quarter circles put together are exactly equivalent to 1 complete circle, so the total dark area is πr^2. The overall radius of the traffic sign is 20 cm, so the total area is π·20^2 = 400π. The area of the light-colored part equals the total area minus the area of the dark part, namely 400π - πr^2. The problem gives that the total dark area is equal to the area of the light-colored part, so πr^2 = 400π - πr^2. Thus 2πr^2 = 400π, r^2 = 200, r = √200 = 10√2. Therefore the radius of this circle is 10√2 cm.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as one circular traffic sign divided into dark regions and the remaining light regions. Let r be the radius of the circle of which each dark piece is a quarter. From the text, the sign has radius 20 cm and the combined area of the 4 dark quarters equals the light part. The 4 quarter-circles together have area equal to one full circle of radius r, namely πr^2. The whole sign has area π·20^2, so the light area is π·20^2 - πr^2. Set πr^2 = π·20^2 - πr^2 and solve for r.
